subject.title: fix(providers): harden recorder and runtime lifecycle

question: Should an existing recorder with a complete schema-invalid tail fail closed on every append, or should Crabline provide a bounded quarantine or repair path during upgrade?
rationale: The stricter validation protects recorder integrity but can turn latent on-disk corruption into a runtime outage, so the permanent compatibility contract requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Add explicit recovery
options.body: Preserve strict validation while adding an actionable quarantine or repair path and upgrade-focused regression coverage for pre-existing malformed tails.

options.title: Accept fail-closed behavior
options.body: Keep unconditional rejection and explicitly own the operator-intervention requirement through clear diagnostics and release context.

options.title: Defer strict rejection
options.body: Land the independent permissions, durability, JWT, and cleanup fixes while postponing malformed-tail rejection until its upgrade policy is settled.

recommendation.title: Add explicit recovery
recommendation.body: Preserve strict validation while adding an actionable quarantine or repair path and upgrade-focused regression coverage for pre-existing malformed tails.

likelyOwner.reason: They implemented the behavior and are the strongest available repository-member owner for explaining its intended compatibility contract.
